preamble: Denasalization of the velar nasal [ŋ] to the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] keeps the velar place and voicing but removes the nasal airflow and turns the closure into a fricative. It is documented in the history of the Inuit languages, where Proto-Eskimo *ŋ became *ɣ before a non-nasal consonant in Proto-Inuit, while the Yupik languages kept the nasal. Inupiaq still shows the fricative, written g, as in iglu 'house'.

examples.from: Proto-Eskimo *əŋlu 'house' (cf. Alutiiq engluq, Central Siberian Yupik nenglu)
examples.note: Before the consonant l, *ŋ lost its nasality and became the velar fricative written g in Inupiaq; Inuvialuktun, Inuinnaqtun and Inuktun iglu agree, while Greenlandic illu shows a later assimilation of the fricative to l. The Yupik descendants keep the nasal.

sources: Fortescue, Michael; Jacobson, Steven; Kaplan, Lawrence (2010). Comparative Eskimo Dictionary with Aleut Cognates, 2nd ed., via Wiktionary (2026). Reconstruction:Proto-Eskimo/əŋlu. https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Reconstruction:Proto-Eskimo/%C9%99%C5%8Blu
